decisions.quote: Using three indices of replicability, our findings did not fully replicate E&S2010 but do corroborate those reported in other replications. While the type of pretraining (Adverb or Verb) strongly biased interpretation and production in E&S2010, this study and other replications found minimal evidence of a distinct Verb pretraining effect on interpretation and production. All studies did confirm strong Adverb pretraining effects, however.
decisions.location: Discussion, Summary of Findings (lines 1236-1244); see also Results (lines 835-837, 880-896, 979-986, 1049-1056, 1176-1184) and Conclusion (lines 1522-1534)
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly frames its own replication results as 'partially replicating E&S2010' across every analysis in the Results section and as having 'not fully replicate[d] E&S2010' in the Summary of Findings because the Adverb pretraining effect (RQ1) was confirmed in both interpretation and production whereas the Verb pretraining effect (RQ2) was not replicated. Even the abstract states that the initial study's findings were not confirmed specifically 'due to performance in verb pretraining'. Because the authors themselves present their evidence as partially replicating the original study (confirming one core tested pretraining effect while failing to confirm the other), the outcome is 'mixed' under the codebook.
